claims.evidence: FDA page: Stelara approved for moderately to severely active UC in paediatric patients aged 2 years and older; news item dated 08/28/2026.
FDA: patients aged 2 years and older with moderately to severely active UC. (Label trial enrolled ages 3-17, but the indication is 2+.)
FDA calls Stelara the first approved therapeutic monoclonal antibody that does not target TNF-alpha for the two main forms of paediatric IBD.
FDA page wording: approved Stelara (ustekinumab) injection for moderately to severely active UC in paediatric patients aged 2 and older.
FDA orphan database entry (designated 02/22/2017) gives marketing approval date 08/28/2026 for paediatric UC.
FDA page states Stelara approved April 15, 2026 for moderately to severely active Crohn's in paediatric patients aged 2+; orphan db shows 04/15/2026.
FDA: first approved therapeutic monoclonal antibody not targeting human TNF-alpha for the two main forms of paediatric IBD.
FDA announcement lists nasopharyngitis, headache, abdominal pain, influenza, fever, diarrhea, sinusitis, fatigue, nausea. The parenthetical gloss 'a common cold' is a lay explanation (textbook).
Orphan database: ustekinumab for paediatric UC, orphan designation 02/22/2017, status Designated/Approved.
